name: cooknest
description:
CookNest is where people keep the recipes they cook: imported from Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and any website, scanned from paper, or typed in. This plugin connects ChatGPT to your own CookNest account so you can work with that library in conversation.

Ask what you can cook with chicken and ChatGPT searches your saved recipes, not the web. Paste a link to a recipe you liked and it is saved to your library with ingredients and steps. Plan the week's dinners from your own recipes, then turn the plan into a shopping list sorted by aisle, skipping the staples you always have at home. Tick items off as you shop, keep private notes on a recipe ("less sugar next time"), and organise recipes into collections.

Everything ChatGPT changes shows up right away in the CookNest app on iPhone, Android and the web. You sign in with your CookNest account (Google, Apple or email). ChatGPT only reaches your own recipes, plans and lists; it never receives your password or payment details, and you can disconnect it at any time.

positive.description: Search the user's own library and show the results as CookNest recipe cards (MCP App view).
positive.prompt: Show me my recipes with chicken.
positive.expected_behavior: A CookNest recipe grid from the user's library for "chicken", led by Chicken Tikka Masala and Chicken Tacos (Chicken Tacos marked as a favorite), with photos and cook times. No web results.

positive.description: Open one recipe by name and show it as a CookNest recipe card.
positive.expected_behavior: The Chicken Tacos recipe card: 4 servings with a servings scaler, 30 min, 10 ingredients starting with 500 g chicken thighs, 5 steps, a Start cooking button, and the private note "Kids prefer it without chilli. Double the lime." No recipe id is needed.

positive.description: Plan a meal (write, ChatGPT asks to confirm) and show the week's plan.
positive.prompt: Put Shakshuka on my meal plan for dinner tomorrow, then show me my week.
positive.expected_behavior: After the user confirms the write, Shakshuka is scheduled for tomorrow's dinner in "My plan", and the CookNest week planner card shows it as the only meal of the week.

positive.description: Turn the week's meal plan into a shopping list (run after the previous case).
positive.prompt: Add everything I need for my planned meals this week to my shopping list.
positive.expected_behavior: The 8 Shakshuka ingredients are added to "My list" grouped by aisle (garlic, onion, parsley, red bell pepper, eggs, ground cumin, sweet paprika, crushed tomatoes) and shown as the CookNest shopping list card. Olive oil and salt are reported as skipped because they are in the pantry.

positive.description: Import a recipe from a link into the user's library.
positive.prompt: Save this recipe to my CookNest: https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/easy-pancakes
positive.expected_behavior: A new recipe "Easy pancakes" is saved to the library and shown as a recipe card with its photo, ingredients and steps. Asking again with the same link returns the existing recipe (already_imported) instead of a duplicate.

negative.description: Recipe that is not in the library: the plugin must not invent one.
negative.prompt: Show me my Laura's birthday cake recipe.

negative.description: Out of scope: CookNest keeps shopping lists but cannot place orders or take payments.
negative.prompt: Order these ingredients for delivery to my home.

negative.description: Bulk destructive request: nothing is deleted without explicit per-action confirmation; there is no bulk delete tool.

review.commerce_description: CookNest does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: First release of CookNest in ChatGPT. It connects ChatGPT to the user's own CookNest account through the CookNest MCP server: search and open saved recipes, import a recipe from a link, create and edit recipes, plan meals for the week, turn a recipe or the week's plan into a shopping list grouped by aisle (skipping pantry staples), tick items off, keep private notes and organise recipes into collections. Interactive CookNest views (MCP Apps) show a recipe grid, a recipe card with servings scaling and cook mode, the week's meal planner and the shopping list.

defaultPrompt: What can I cook tonight with the chicken in my fridge?
Plan dinners for this week using my recipes, nothing too long on weekdays.
Add everything I need for my planned meals this week to my shopping list.
